subject: Bespoke token crediting, exit-protection & stepdown pricing — Orion Systems RFP response
messages:
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@orionsystems.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, procurement@orionsystems.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP commercial ask — usage variability and safe exit protections

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of Orion's RFP we need a compact commercial response that specifically addresses:

- How you structure token pricing when usage can ramp up quickly and then fall (example: pilot -> national roll-out -> pause).
- Commitment mechanics that balance unit economics for us and risk for Redwood (monthly commits, shelfing, true-ups).
- Overages vs. committed rates and how reconciliations happen.
- Early-exit protections (we may pilot for 12 months then pause or wind down). Can you propose an approach that gives us liquidity protection and predictable economics?

Please include an example blended rate table for typical query patterns, a short early-exit term sheet (credits/escrow) and any operational constraints (minimum notice, invoice cadence).

Appreciate a PDF term sheet we can circulate to procurement/legal.

Best,
Emily
Emily Ross
Head of Procurement, Orion Systems
em: emily.ross@orionsystems.com
ph: +1 415-555-0132

---
P.S. Attached is our high-level monthly traffic profile (for context) — please assume seasonality with a peak in months 4-6.

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@orionsystems.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 13:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP commercial ask — usage variability and safe exit protections

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic file. Attached is a compact term sheet and an illustrative pricing workbook. Summary below (high level, negotiable):

1) Pricing (per 1k token equivalents, model-agnostic tiers)
- Base generation (opt-quant models): $2.25 per 1k tokens at list
- Large context / fine-tuned variants (+20%): $2.70 per 1k tokens
- Embeddings (per 1k tokens): $0.80 per 1k tokens

2) Commitment structure options (choose one):
A) Monthly Reserved Commit (recommended for predictable throughput)
  - Commit band (monthly): $50k / $150k / $400k
  - Committed units are invoiced monthly at a 12% discount to list (applied to committed consumption).
  - Overage (consumption above commit in a month): charged at 125% of list for that model class.
B) Shelfed Commit (hybrid for pilot-to-rollouts)
  - Unused committed tokens can be carried forward ("shelfed") for up to 6 months; carried units draw down before incurring overage.
  - Shelfing preserves discount but cannot exceed 50% of a single month's commit in a given month.

3) Liquidity & Exit Protection (term-sheet proposal)
- Exit Escrow Credit: Redwood will set aside an escrow equal to 10% of the annual committed value (collected over first 3 invoices) that converts to a credit against final invoice if customer terminates after >= 90 days.
- Early Termination: If Orion terminates with < 12 months remaining, remaining committed spend is payable, offset by escrow credit.
- Mid-contract Ramp-down: For step reductions >25% compared to baseline commit, customer may trigger a renegotiation window (30 days) or pay a stepdown fee equal to 2 months' average committed value.

4) True-up & Reconciliation
- Quarterly true-ups: actual consumption vs. committed are reconciled each quarter. If consumption < committed, unused committed units (beyond shelf allowances) convert to account credits. If consumption > committed historically, overages are billed at month-of-use rates.

5) Reporting & Operational Constraints
- Usage reporting: daily per-model token breakdown via S3/secure link.
- Minimum notice for large commit changes: 30 days; for termination: 90 days.
- SLA: 99.5% platform uptime for Dedicated customers; hosted customers have best-effort with credits for sustained outages (see term sheet).

6) Example calculation (monthly):
- Orion picks $150k/month commit (12% discounted committed rate). Assume baseline consumption = 120k USD worth tokens -> you use 80% of commit; 20% is shelfed/credited per policy. If you hit a 150% spike, overage billed at 125% of list for extra units.

Next steps: please review the attached PDF (redwood_term_sheet_exit_escrow_v1.pdf). If agreeable, we can circulate to legal and initiate a DocuSign path for the term sheet. Happy to jump on a 30 min call with procurement + finance to walk through numbers.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP commercial ask — internal note on shelfing and escrow sizing

Quick internal: a couple of suggested tweaks before we send to legal/procurement —

- Escrow sizing: 10% of annual committed value is ok for mid-market, but for larger enterprise deals (>$1.2M ARR) we should tier escrow to 6% after $1.2M to avoid overcapitalization.
- Shelfing guardrails: limit shelfing to 6 months total and cap rolled forward units at 40% of monthly commit for deals where peak is >3x baseline. This reduces risk of long tail liabilities.
- Add a clause: "mid-contract repricing trigger" — if per-token list costs materially increase (GPU spot disruption / licensing) we can invoke a capped pass-through after notice and a 60-day review.

Also propose we offer a one-time onboarding credit (5% of first 3 months commit) for pilot customers to offset early attrition risk. Thoughts?

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Strategy, Redwood

From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@orionsystems.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orionsystems.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP commercial ask — usage variability and safe exit protections

Vanessa / Karthik — thanks, the level of detail is helpful. Procurement and finance reviewed the PDF and had two quick asks before we circulate to legal: 

1) Can the escrow be structured as a refundable credit (applied to final invoice) rather than a cash escrow? That will simplify our treasury approval.
2) Can Redwood add a hard cap on stepdown fees (example: no more than 2 months committed spend or $200k, whichever is lower)?

If you can confirm those two items and re-issue the term sheet, procurement will slot the term sheet for legal review and we can aim for a decision window in 14 days.

Appreciate the quick turn — we expect to select a vendor by end of month.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Ross
Head of Procurement, Orion Systems
